newsitem.title: CHINA: Peugeot to stay in China after end of JV.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot to stay in China after end of JV.

text.p: French automaker PSA Peugeot Citroen will push its Peugeot brand in China even after its expected withdrawal from a foundering joint venture in the southern city of Guangzhou, a company official said on Wednesday.

Peugeot's nationwide after-sales network and a base of more than 100,000 customers meant there was an assured future for the brand in China's potentially huge car market, said the official, who declined to be identified.
Chinese officials have said they are seeking a new partner to take PSA Peugeot Citroen's 30 percent stake in Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile, which ceased production several months ago.
General Motors Corp said in May it had been selected by Beijing to draft plans for small car assembly at the Guangzhou venture.

PSA Peugeot Citroen has said it aims to focus production in the central city of Wuhan, where Citroen has a joint venture making a variant of its ZX sedan, but the Peugeot official said his brand would also have a role to play.
"The main thing is to be in China -- and we are in China," he said at a Beijing motor show, where Peugeot put on a display of new cars that made no mention of the company's Chinese-made models.

The Guangzhou venture had long been criticised for producing cars little changed in design from the 1980s, and the official said it was important to boost Peugeot's image in China. "We are here to show that Peugeot cars are modern and stylish," he said.
Peugeot had already imported some vehicles into China and was confident that such sales would grow, despite tariffs and taxes that boosted prices by from 110 to 180 percent, he said.
"It's difficult to import... but there are people who are ready to pay and who can afford it," he said. "The import market will grow."
Peugeot was also ready to consider future production ventures in China, he said but gave no details.
Officials at a separate display vaunting the output of Citroen's Wuhan venture with China's Dongfeng Automotive Group said the French firm expected a rapid rise in output over the next few years.

Dongfeng-Citroen Automobile Co Ltd would sell all the 30,000 Fukang sedans it expected to produce this year and planned to boost production to 60,000 in 1998 and to double it again the year after, said venture sales chief Hugues Lacord.

Dongfeng officials said last year that high costs and low prices meant the joint venture lost about 10,000 yuan ($1,200) on each Fukang it sold, but Lacord said he was confident the Chinese ZX variant would become a more economic product.
"In one year (we) will be able to make money on each unit," he said. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
